subject: [PATCH 00/10] mm/madvise: refactor cold and pageout page table walks

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the number of self-tests and their purpose, explaining that they were originally 28 individual commits but were squashed for initial review. They clarify that some tests may need adjustment after a valid kernel implementation change and intentionally assert splitting, PMD/PTE mapping shape, folio flags or folio sharing.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT page-walk callback is named after its PTE implementation, agreed to rename it to madvise_lru_pmd_entry() before separating PMD and PTE paths, and stated that no functional change is intended.
sentiment_signals: agreed to make a non-functional change

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the PMD callback still handles PTE table mapping and unmapping, splitting, and rescheduling after dispatching huge PMDs, which mixes PTE lock ownership with page-walk callback. They moved this lifecycle into madvise_lru_pte_range(), which drops the lock before splitting or yielding, leaving the PMD callback to select the huge-PMD or PTE path. No functional change is intended.

2026-09-22.patch_summary: This patch refactors the code responsible for handling MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT page table walks to improve maintainability and auditability. The original implementation was a complex nest of functions, which led to bugs being introduced frequently. To address this issue, the patch separates the handling of huge PMDs, PTE batching, PTE-lock ownership, and shared walk setup into distinct functions. Additionally, 28 self-tests are included to ensure that the refactored code does not introduce new issues. The patch aims to simplify the control flow and make it easier to audit page-table lock ownership and split retries.

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Lorenzo (ARM) expressed concerns about the large size of the patch and suggested splitting it into smaller parts based on logical test areas.

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Lorenzo (ARM) noted that the huge-PMD and PTE paths duplicate common filtering and LRU operations, obscuring page-table-specific control flow, and requested factoring these into helpers to improve clarity.

> The MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT page-walk callback is named after its PTE
> implementation even though it is registered as a PMD callback and serves
> both LRU operations.
>
> Rename it to madvise_lru_pmd_entry() before separating the PMD and PTE
> paths.
>
> No functional change intended.
>
> Assisted-by: LLM
> Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>

Oh yeah wow I was thinking 'reasonable in that it is the PTE range which the PMD
entry spans' but err, no, it does handle THP PMDs too so :)

And LRU is a resonable name, it does seem to me that these are the only madvise
operations that qualify so all makes sense.

So:

Cheers, Lorenzo

2026-09-23.patch_summary: This patch refactors the code responsible for handling MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT page table walks to improve maintainability and auditability. The original implementation was a complex nest of functions, which led to bugs being introduced frequently. To address this issue, the patch separates the handling of huge PMDs, PTE batching, PTE-lock ownership, and shared walk setup into distinct functions. Additionally, 28 self-tests are included to ensure that the refactored code does not introduce new issues. The patch aims to simplify the control flow and make it easier to audit page-table lock ownership and split retries.

2026-09-24.patch_summary: This patch refactors the code responsible for handling MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT page table walks to improve maintainability and auditability. The original implementation was a complex nest of functions, which led to bugs being introduced frequently. To address this issue, the patch separates the handling of huge PMDs, PTE batching, PTE-lock ownership, and shared walk setup into distinct functions. Additionally, 28 self-tests are included to ensure that the refactored code does not introduce new issues. The patch aims to simplify the control flow and make it easier to audit page-table lock ownership and split retries.
